item.title: FAA sees $100 million impact from tariffs on air traffic control modernization plan
item.description: The head of the Federal Aviation Administration said the agency expects about a $100 million impact from tariffs on the government's more than $12.5 billion air traffic control modernization plan.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The head of the Federal Aviation Administration said the agency expects about a $100 million impact from tariffs on the government's more than $12.5 billion air traffic control modernization plan. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the $100 million was in total for modernization efforts and said two radar suppliers Raytheon and Indra Group were moving radar production to US facilities in Florida and Kansas City respectively.

item.title: EEUU da luz verde a venta de aviones militares por24.300 millones de dólares a Arabia Saudita
item.description: El Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos ha aprobado la posible venta a Arabia Saudita de aviones de combate F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter de Lockheed Martin , informó el jueves, en un momento en que el reino se ve cada vez más envuelto en la guerra de Oriente Medio.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos ha aprobado la posible venta a Arabia Saudita de aviones de combate F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter de Lockheed Martin (LMT.N) , informó el jueves, en un momento en que el reino se ve cada vez más envuelto en la guerra de Oriente Medio. La venta, estimada en 24.300 millones de dólares, incluiría 48 de estos aviones militares y 49 motores Pratt & Whitney, además de equipos de comunicaciones, piezas de recambio y otros artículos de apoyo, según indicó el departamento. "La venta propuesta de este equipamiento y estos servicios de apoyo no alterará el equilibrio militar en la región", señaló en un comunicado publicado en internet.

item.title: Two US-bound vessels apparently compromised by hackers, US officials say
item.description: US Coast Guard and FBI personnel boarded two commercial vessels bound for the United States in the Gulf of Mexico last month after indications that hackers had broken into their computer networks, the agencies said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter, Jonathan Saul
item.content:encoded: US Coast Guard and FBI personnel boarded two commercial vessels bound for the United States in the Gulf of Mexico last month after indications that hackers had broken into their computer networks, the agencies said on Thursday. The unusual operation, carried out on August 21 and August 24 aboard two foreign-flagged ships, comes as US authorities grapple with a series of cyber incidents that media reports have linked to Iran since the outbreak of conflict between Washington and Tehran. The FBI said a joint Coast Guard-FBI team boarded the vessels after receiving "indications that the networks of both vessels were compromised." The Coast Guard, which referred only to the August 21 boarding, said that "foreign cyber actors" were involved but did not identify them. Neither agency provided further details about the incidents or explained the discrepancies between their accounts. The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency did not immediately return a message seeking comment. Corey Ranslem, CEO of maritime security group Dryad Global, said that his firm had confirmed that one of the ships was the Liberian-flagged VL Prosperity. The vessel is currently anchored in waters around Galveston in Texas, according to LSEG and MarineTraffic ship tracking data. Liberia’s flag registry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Iran's Mehr news agency reported on August 20 that VL Prosperity had suffered what it called "a major cyberattack" while transiting through the Strait of Gibraltar and that its communications had been knocked out for 30 hours. Citing an unnamed crew member, Mehr reported that hackers had also infiltrated the engine-room systems, reduced the engine’s cooling flow, increased the engine speed, and disabled the ship’s fuel and engine-oil tank. The Iranian news agency did not say who was thought to be behind the alleged attack. Although dramatic in its effects, a ship-centered cyberattack is not that difficult to pull off, Ranslem said. "We are expecting these types of attacks to continue and will expand in the very near future," he said.

item.title: King Charles sounded like 'lottery winner' after Diana's death, her brother writes
item.description: Britain's King Charles sounded "like a lottery winner" after the death of his late first wife Diana, her brother writes in his forthcoming book, new extracts of which were published on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain's King Charles sounded "like a lottery winner" after the death of his late first wife Diana, her brother writes in his forthcoming book, new extracts of which were published on Thursday. Diana's brother Charles Spencer said the then-Prince Charles was "giddily elated" in the immediate aftermath of Diana's death in 1997, possibly because he felt it meant he was freer to marry again, according to passages in the Daily Mail. Charles on Wednesday took the [USN:L8N4581JE TEXT:"unusual step of responding"] to criticism after the first extracts of Spencer's book were published in the Daily Mail, saying via a spokesperson that grief could impact reason, judgment and memory. There was no new comment from the king on the latest excerpts, which also stated that Diana went to a site of many suicides on Britain's south coast, but that her love for her sons, William and Harry, "stopped her from going further". "It is a sad fact that, in her later years, Diana drove herself more than once to Beachy Head, the highest chalk sea cliff in England, while contemplating ending it all," Spencer wrote. Diana was killed at the age of 36 when the car carrying her and her lover Dodi al-Fayed crashed in Paris as it sped away from chasing paparazzi photographers on motorbikes. Spencer says in the book that he spoke to Charles shortly after Diana's death was confirmed, writing: "Unlike my other callers, who were stunned, barely able to articulate their condolences and offers of help, he sounded giddily elated – like a lottery winner, I remember thinking at the time." Spencer added: "Looking back now, I suspect the prince's first reaction must have been to think more of how this event might free him to marry the woman he loved, rather than appreciating the loss of one he did not." Charles and Diana separated in 1992 and divorced in 1996. That was a year after Diana told the BBC that "there were three of us in this marriage, so it was a bit crowded" in reference to Charles' relationship with Camilla Parker Bowles, whom he married in 2005. A Buckingham Palace spokesperson said on Wednesday: "While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss."

item.title: GM reforça aposta em picapes a diesel enquanto concorrentes investem em híbridos
item.description: A General Motors está mantendo o motor a diesel para maximizar a eficiência de combustível ao lançar sua picape de nova geração, diferenciando-se das ofertas híbridas dos concorrentes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A General Motors (GM.N) está mantendo o motor a diesel para maximizar a eficiência de combustível ao lançar sua picape de nova geração, diferenciando-se das ofertas híbridas dos concorrentes. A GM planeja lançar no quarto trimestre a primeira grande reformulação desde 2019 de seus veículos mais importantes: as picapes Chevrolet Silverado e GMC Sierra. Juntas, elas são os modelos mais vendidos da montadora de Detroit em todo o mundo e representam a maior parte dos lucros da empresa. Para melhorar a economia de combustível, a GM anunciou na quinta-feira que as caminhonetes oferecerão um motor a diesel aprimorado que, combinado com um tanque de combustível maior opcional, proporcionará uma autonomia em rodovia de mais de 900 milhas antes de precisar reabastecer. Os principais concorrentes da GM no segmento de picapes leves, a Ford (F.N) e a Stellantis, fabricante da Ram (STLAM.MI) , estão apostando em híbridos para obter a máxima eficiência de combustível de suas picapes. A GM, por outro lado, tem evitado os híbridos ao longo dos anos. "É um pouco diferente de adicionar um sistema híbrido a um conjunto motopropulsor existente e tentar extrair eficiência de algo assim", disse o presidente da GM, Mark Reuss, sobre o motor a diesel de 3,0 litros durante uma coletiva de imprensa. Reuss reconheceu os altos preços do diesel, que ultrapassaram US$6 por galão na semana passada, um recorde histórico. Ele fez uma distinção entre picos temporários de preços decorrentes de eventos geopolíticos e aumentos estruturais, e afirmou que a GM está apostando na eficiência superior dos motores a diesel a longo prazo. No início desta década, a Ford descontinuou o motor a diesel da sua F-150 em favor de um modelo híbrido, que, segundo a empresa, oferecia uma melhor combinação de potência e economia de combustível. Um porta-voz afirmou na quinta-feira: "Vamos fazer o que é certo para os clientes da F-150, independentemente do que a concorrência diga ou faça." VEÍCULOS A DIESEL TÊM MELHOR RENDIMENTO POR GALÃO, MAS SÃO MAIS CAROS A reformulação da Silverado e da Sierra pela GM marca, extraoficialmente, a próxima fase da longa batalha de Detroit no mercado de picapes. A Ford deve lançar a próxima geração da sua F-150 em 2028, segundo previsões. A GM, a Ford e a Stellantis representam mais de 90% das vendas no lucrativo mercado norte-americano de picapes grandes e competem acirradamente pelo direito de se destacar em métricas de desempenho, como capacidade de reboque e economia de combustível. Os motores a diesel geralmente oferecem melhor eficiência de combustível em rodovias do que os motores a gasolina, razão pela qual caminhões de carga de grande porte normalmente utilizam motores a diesel. Cada uma das montadoras de Detroit oferece motores a diesel em suas picapes maiores e mais robustas, como a Super Duty da Ford e a Ram 2500. Mas suas abordagens divergiram em relação às picapes menores: a F-150 da Ford, as Silverado e Sierra, e a 1500 da Ram. Segundo a recomendação federal, a picape híbrida 4x4 da Ford faz uma média de 23 milhas por galão (aproximadamente 9,8 km/l). Já as versões atuais da GM Silverado e Sierra, com tração nas quatro rodas e motor a diesel, alcançam 24 mpg (aproximadamente 10,2 km/l). No entanto, como o preço do diesel costuma ser mais alto que o da gasolina, os proprietários das picapes da GM gastariam cerca de US$ 1.050 por ano, considerando 15.000 milhas (aproximadamente 24.000 km) percorridas, de acordo com a estimativa federal. A Ram tem planos para uma picape híbrida de alcance estendido, um tipo de híbrido plug-in que, segundo a empresa, terá uma autonomia de 690 milhas (aproximadamente 1.110 km). A GM também afirmou que as picapes Silverado e Sierra redesenhadas terão dois novos motores V-8, maiores e mais potentes que os modelos anteriores, com menores emissões de escapamento. (Por Kalea Hall)

item.title: Identifican en Bolivia a una nueva especie de gato, la primera en más de un siglo
item.description: Un pequeño felino salvaje que habita en el bosque nuboso de Bolivia ha sido identificado como una especie hasta ahora desconocida, lo que supone la primera vez en más de un siglo en que se bautiza y describe formalmente un nuevo felino vivo.
item.dc:creator: Marta Serafinko
item.content:encoded: Un pequeño felino salvaje que habita en el bosque nuboso de Bolivia ha sido identificado como una especie hasta ahora desconocida, lo que supone la primera vez en más de un siglo en que se bautiza y describe formalmente un nuevo felino vivo. El felino, llamado "Tilcayo" por las comunidades locales, forma parte de un grupo denominado "gatos tigre", que se encuentra en gran parte de Sudamérica. El tilcayo fue hallado en el frondoso bosque de los Yungas de Bolivia, una región montañosa donde los árboles suelen estar cubiertos por nubes y hay mucha humedad, según los investigadores. Mide unos 46 centímetros de largo y pesa alrededor de 1,4 kilos, es decir, es más pequeño que un gato doméstico promedio. Los investigadores usaron datos genéticos para confirmar que el felino es una nueva especie y le dieron el nombre científico de "Leopardus tilcayo", conservando así su nombre local. "Su pelaje es de color marrón claro (…) con rosetas de forma irregular repartidas por todo el cuerpo", explicó Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, exploradora de National Geographic y una de las autoras del estudio que describe la especie recién identificada y que se publicó el jueves en la revista Current Biology. Aún se sabe poco sobre la biología y el modo de vida de este felino. Los restos de pequeños roedores encontrados en muestras de excrementos sugieren que podrían formar parte de su dieta, mientras que las pruebas obtenidas con cámaras trampa indican que podría ser más activo por la noche, señaló Nogales-Ascarrunz. Los gatos tigre son lo que se denomina "especies crípticas", lo que significa que no se pueden distinguir fácilmente solo por su aspecto, explicó el biólogo evolutivo y coautor principal del estudio Jonas Lescroart, de la Universidad de Amberes, en Bélgica. Antes, los gatos tigre se consideraban una única especie, pero estudios genéticos realizados hace décadas sugirieron la existencia de múltiples especies. "Nuestra información, en este momento, se limita a los dos ejemplares vivos que examinamos y a un pequeño número de registros de cámaras trampa", dijo Lescroart sobre la nueva especie. Uno de los felinos vivos es un macho de 10 años que ahora vive en el Santuario de Vida Silvestre Senda Verde, tras haber sido criado por una familia local en su hogar. "UN ANIMAL DIFERENTE" La observación del gato boliviano despertó interés porque "sus características no coincidían con las descripciones, la mayoría de ellas basadas en gatos brasileños", explicó Nogales-Ascarrunz. "Esto nos llevó a preguntarnos: ¿qué tipo de gato tigre hay realmente en Bolivia?". El equipo analizó el ADN de 38 gatos de los que se habían tomado muestras en varios países sudamericanos, incluidos ocho especímenes de museo. El estudio reveló que los gatos tigre son, de hecho, cinco especies genéticamente distintas. "Nunca esperábamos que este gato tigre boliviano fuera una especie aparte, y nadie lo había propuesto nunca como un animal diferente, ya fuera una subespecie o de otro tipo", contó Lescroart. El análisis genético sugirió que el linaje de Tilcayo se separó de otros gatos tigre hace aproximadamente 1,4 millones de años. "Cuantas más diferencias hay en su ADN, más tiempo estimamos que llevan separados físicamente esos linajes", explicó Lescroart, que añadió que, en el caso de los gatos, tal brecha se considera generalmente una división de especie. El equipo de investigación también describió una nueva subespecie de gato tigre en los Yungas peruanos, a la que denominó Leopardus tigrinus antisuyo, en honor a Antisuyu, la región del antiguo Imperio Inca que abarcaba el área en la que habita. La Lista Roja de la Unión Internacional para la Conservación de la Naturaleza (UICN), que realiza un seguimiento del estado de las especies, clasifica actualmente a los gatos tigre como dos especies "vulnerables" con poblaciones en declive. Los investigadores han compartido sus hallazgos con la UICN, cuya próxima revisión evaluará los cinco linajes por separado. Esto podría ofrecer una imagen más precisa del riesgo, señaló Lescroart, y especies como el tilcayo podrían llegar a considerarse en peligro de extinción si se evalúan de forma independiente. La necesidad de una evaluación más clara es especialmente acuciante en los Yungas, uno de los ecosistemas más amenazados de la región.

item.title: Canadian dollar steadies near six-week low as interest rate spreads widen
item.description: The Canadian dollar steadied near a six-week low against its US counterpart on Thursday and bond yields fell, with a wider gap between the interest rates set by the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Canada helping to underpin the greenback.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: The Canadian dollar steadied near a six-week low against its US counterpart on Thursday and bond yields fell, with a wider gap between the interest rates set by the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Canada helping to underpin the greenback. The loonie was trading nearly unchanged at 1.3985 per US dollar, or 71.51 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since August 7 at 1.4001. The Fed on Wednesday [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"raised its benchmark interest rate"] by a quarter of a percentage point to the 3.75%-4.00% range and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in coming months. Earlier this month, the Bank of Canada left its key rate unchanged at 2.25%. "The interest differential between the US and Canada is certainly providing the support for the US dollar," Darren Richardson, chief operating officer at Vantry Capital Inc, said in a note. "The 1.40 level is a key technical level in the short term," Richardson added. The price of oil, one of Canada's major exports, edged lower as reports of additional Saudi crude cargoes through Oman eased supply concerns. US crude oil futures were trading down 0.3% at $102.16 a barrel. Domestic data showed that [USN:AQN2MJNYS TEXT:"foreign investors"] bought a net C$20.65 billion ($14.76 billion) in Canadian securities in July, led by federal government bonds, following an upwardly revised C$41.25 billion total purchase in June, while Canadian investors sold a net C$30.63 billion worth of foreign securities. The Canadian 10-year yield was down 9.3 basis points at 3.848%. It fell 4.7 basis points further below the equivalent US rate to a gap of about 111 basis points. That gap is the widest since June 2025. [USN:L1N45906M TEXT:"Canada and Europe"] should ally to protect their markets, democracies and rule of law in a world dominated by the US and China, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said, after an EU proposal to make Canada an "associate member."

item.title: US clears way for $24.3 billion military aircraft sale to Saudi Arabia
item.description: The US Department of State has approved the potential sale of Lockheed Martin's F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter aircraft to Saudi Arabia, it said on Thursday as the kingdom has been drawn deeper into the Middle East war.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Department of State has approved the potential sale of Lockheed Martin's (LMT.N) F-35 Lightning II Joint Strike Fighter aircraft to Saudi Arabia, it said on Thursday as the kingdom has been drawn deeper into the [USN:L4N45908T TEXT:"Middle East war"]. The estimated $24.3 billion sale would include 48 of the military aircraft and 49 Pratt & Whitney engines along with communications equipment, spare parts and other support items, the department said. "The proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the military balance in the region," it said in a notice posted online.

item.title: Deputados democratas buscam impedir acordo nuclear de Trump com Arábia Saudita
item.description: Os democratas da Câmara dos Deputados dos EUA manifestaram preocupação nesta quinta-feira com o acordo nuclear civil do presidente Donald Trump com a Arábia Saudita e afirmaram ter apresentado uma resolução de desaprovação com o objetivo de impedir que o acordo entre em vigor.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: Os democratas da Câmara dos Deputados dos EUA manifestaram preocupação nesta quinta-feira com o acordo nuclear civil do presidente Donald Trump com a Arábia Saudita e afirmaram ter apresentado uma resolução de desaprovação com o objetivo de impedir que o acordo entre em vigor. Trump enviou a proposta de acordo ao Congresso em agosto, abrindo um prazo de 90 dias para análise pelos parlamentares e dando a eles a oportunidade de tentar aprovar uma resolução de desaprovação. Democratas e defensores da não proliferação criticaram o pacto nuclear por não impedir a Arábia Saudita de enriquecer urânio ou reprocessar resíduos nucleares, dois caminhos potenciais para a obtenção de uma arma nuclear. Os Emirados Árabes Unidos concordaram com tais medidas, conhecidas como o “padrão-ouro”, em seu acordo nuclear civil de 2009 com Washington. “Uma região já assolada por conflitos e escaladas não precisa de mais uma potência nuclear”, afirmaram quatro democratas — Gregory Meeks, de Nova York, líder democrata na Comissão de Relações Exteriores da Câmara; Brad Sherman e John Garamendi, da Califórnia; e Don Beyer, da Virgínia — em um comunicado. O governo Trump afirma que o acordo contém as medidas de não proliferação exigidas por lei. Não está claro se a Arábia Saudita conseguirá fechar o acordo sem normalizar as relações com Israel. Trump afirmou que o pacto só entrará em vigor se Riad o fizer, mas assessores do Congresso disseram que não há nada no acordo que trate dessa questão. Membros do Congresso também pediram que todo o acordo — incluindo as “cartas paralelas” confidenciais firmadas com a Arábia Saudita — seja divulgado publicamente. O acordo nuclear de 30 anos prevê a construção de reatores AP1000, um projeto no valor de dezenas de bilhões de dólares que beneficiaria a Westinghouse, de propriedade conjunta da Cameco, com sede no Canadá (CCO.TO) , e da Brookfield Asset Management (BAM.N) . Não está claro quando a Câmara poderá votar a resolução. O presidente da Câmara, Mike Johnson, dispensou os deputados na quarta-feira até depois das eleições de meio de mandato de 3 de novembro. Além disso, embora o Congresso tenha aprovado dezenas de resoluções de reprovação ao longo dos anos, nenhuma resolução relativa à energia nuclear ou à cooperação nuclear civil jamais foi aprovada com sucesso. De acordo com a Seção 123 da Lei de Energia Atômica de 1954, os acordos de cooperação nuclear para fins pacíficos entram automaticamente em vigor após 90 dias, caso o Congresso não tenha aprovado uma resolução de desaprovação para bloqueá-los.

item.title: Will AI fears reach the ballot box?
item.description: Hello, I’m Nandita Bose, a White House correspondent for Reuters. I’ve spent much of the past two decades reporting on power, first through the lens of companies and corporate investigations and, since 2019, through national politics and the White House. After spending last week at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, I returned to Washington to find the capital in an uproar over the potential threat of artificial intelligence. It got me thinking about how quickly an issue can move from policy debate to a campaign talking point, and then into a concern that voters weigh at the ballot box. Whether AI becomes a voting issue in November remains unclear, but it is moving rapidly in that direction.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose
item.content:encoded: Hello, I’m Nandita Bose, a White House correspondent for Reuters. I’ve spent much of the past two decades reporting on power, first through the lens of companies and corporate investigations and, since 2019, through national politics and the White House. After spending last week at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, I returned to Washington to find the capital in an uproar over the potential threat of artificial intelligence. It got me thinking about how quickly an issue can move from policy debate to a campaign talking point, and then into a concern that voters weigh at the ballot box. Whether AI becomes a voting issue in November remains unclear, but it is moving rapidly in that direction. And, in July, we asked you to submit your questions about the midterms. This week we will start answering them by focusing on one topic every week. The questions were grouped into six main ones that were assigned to our US-based reporters with the relevant experience. Scroll down for my colleague Joseph Ax's answer to your questions about voter eligibility verification. When I was talking to Republican voters at the [USN:L4N44W0P3 TEXT:"convention"], AI mostly came up in the context of everyday costs: power bills, water use and whether the data centers popping up around the country were going to make life more expensive. Then, in a matter of days, AI went from a [USN:L6N43G12P TEXT:"debate over data centers"] and household costs to a growing argument over whether humanity survives. The existential risk conversation had been building for years, but [USN:L1N45403P TEXT:"fresh warnings"] from [USN:L6N4520JA TEXT:"AI researchers"] and top industry leaders, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI founder Elon Musk, about powerful AI systems becoming difficult to control made it more urgent. Washington is usually late to the party on most topics, but the prospect of human extinction [USN:L6N4560X5 TEXT:"got attention fast"]. Senator Bernie Sanders, a progressive independent, and Steve Bannon, a close ally of President Donald Trump, spoke [USN:L6N45616D TEXT:"at the same event"] calling for AI guardrails. Campaigns are scrambling to figure out where they stand, and Democratic and Republican lawmakers are weighing new restrictions. Trump, meanwhile, suggested that [USN:FWN4560E8 TEXT:"he was the only AI guardrail"] the country needed. “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” he wrote on Truth Social, while arguing that efforts to slow AI development would benefit China. What is unclear is what voters think about all of this. A New York Times/Siena poll found 61% of likely voters opposed building new AI data centers, but AI and data centers barely registered when voters were asked what mattered most to their midterm vote. The cost of living, the economy, immigration and foreign wars remain much more immediate political concerns. That gets at the strange politics of AI right now. There is plenty of unease, but it has not yet settled into a single political argument or become a clearly salient midterm issue. Different parts of the debate are resonating with different voters, making it harder for campaigns to know what message, if any, will stick. With more than six weeks until Election Day, AI could still become a bigger midterm issue. Even if it does not, the fight could loom much larger by the 2028 presidential election as the technology advances, data centers spread, and Washington is forced to decide how much or how little to regulate it. For now, the debate is still taking shape. Americans are talking about it, but many are still figuring out which warnings are grounded in reality and which are political hallucination and whether any of it matters enough to shape their vote. TOP US POLITICS HEADLINES [USN:S0N431004 TEXT:"In loss for Trump, US Supreme Court won’t let Postal Service restrict mail ballots"] Election officials prepare for chaos as Trump seeks to tilt the midterms to Republicans [USN:L6N4520XW TEXT:"Deep in Trump country, a revolt against corporate money could reshape political spending"] [USN:L8N4571L6 TEXT:"Trump administration plans $2.8 billion munitions sale to Israel"] How Trump’s war on EVs derailed America’s auto-factory revival [USN:L6N456110 TEXT:"Noncitizens accused of illegal US voting challenge Trump's authority to prosecute them"] POLL OF THE WEEK YOUR QUESTIONS ABOUT VOTER ELIGIBILITY VERIFICATION What procedures do states use to verify voter eligibility and citizenship, and what does the available evidence show about the frequency and detection of ineligible voting or other election fraud? Answer by Joseph Ax, National Affairs Correspondent Under federal law, every state must retain a statewide list of registered voters and perform regular maintenance on it to remove ineligible voters. In addition, U.S. law requires first-time voters in federal elections who registered by mail to show some form of identification at the polls, such as a driver’s license, a paycheck or a utility bill. Many states have imposed additional, more stringent procedures to verify eligibility, such as photo ID requirements, and those policies vary significantly among states. Votes cast by mail, which have come under frequent baseless attacks from Trump as unreliable, are typically checked by comparing the signature on the envelope with the one on file. All available evidence indicates that ineligible voting, including noncitizen voting, is exceedingly rare. A Reuters investigation this year found just 129 cases in which noncitizens were federally charged with voting illegally; many appeared to stem from voter confusion or administrative errors, rather than intentional fraud. The conservative Heritage Foundation think tank maintains a voter fraud database that includes just 1,619 cases from 1982 to 2025, or one for every 817,625 votes cast in a presidential election during that time. THE VIEW FROM EUROPE Europe is looking for [USN:S8N4150LY TEXT:"new ways to deepen ties"] with like-minded allies as tensions with Washington grow. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen this week proposed opening the door for Canada to become the EU’s first “associate member,” saying new partnerships were needed in what she called an “openly hostile world.” The proposal comes as both the EU and Canada face trade pressure from Trump and seek more room to act independently. For Europe, the push is also part of a broader effort to build stronger partnerships on trade, defense, technology and supply chains as global alliances shift. WHAT TO WATCH FOR September 21: World leaders begin to arrive for the UN General Assembly in New York September 22: Trump expected to address the UN General Assembly September 24: Trump to host Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House THE WHO, WHAT AND WHEN [USN:L6N4510WH TEXT:"ICE arrests keep soaring. Here’s why they are not leading to more deportations"] [USN:L6N4530XO TEXT:"Iran war cost hits $38 billion, forecast to rise $3 billion a month"]

item.title: Acciones europeas suben tras alza de tasas de la Fed, crudo cae y retornos de deuda se estabilizan
item.description: Las acciones europeas subieron el jueves, ya que la bajada de los precios del petróleo y una pausa en la ola de ventas de bonos a nivel mundial impulsaron el apetito por el riesgo tras el esperado aumento de las tasas de interés que aplicó la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos en la víspera.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: Las acciones europeas subieron el jueves, ya que la bajada de los precios del petróleo y una pausa en la ola de ventas de bonos a nivel mundial impulsaron el apetito por el riesgo tras el esperado aumento de las tasas de interés que aplicó la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos en la víspera. * El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) ganó un 0,9%, a 642,6 puntos, en una jornada en la que la mayoría de los mercados regionales registraron avances. * Las acciones de las empresas mineras metalíferas (.SXPP) lideraron las alzas, con un repunte del 2,1%. Las automotrices (.SXAP) subieron un 1,7%, impulsadas por los avances de alrededor del 2% registrados por BMW (BMWG.DE) , Renault (RENA.PA) y Volkswagen . * El crudo Brent amplió sus pérdidas por segundo día consecutivo tras conocerse que Arabia Saudita está ofreciendo cargamentos adicionales a través de Omán, aunque los precios seguían por encima de los 100 dólares el barril. No obstante, el sector energético europeo (.SXEP) avanzó un 0,1%. * La primera subida de tasas de la Fed en tres años reforzó las expectativas de que los principales bancos centrales están intensificando sus esfuerzos para frenar la inflación. El retorno de los bonos del Tesoro caía, mientras los inversores evalúan la decisión y las señales de un mayor endurecimiento monetario en el futuro. * Los inversores también centraban su atención en el Banco de Inglaterra, que mantuvo las tasas sin cambios, al tiempo que advirtió que el aumento vertiginoso de los costos energéticos intensificará las presiones inflacionistas. El FTSE 100 británico (.FTSE) mejoró un 1,2%, su mayor alza diaria en más de dos meses. * Entre otras acciones, Berentzen (BEZ.DE) se disparó un 19,4% después de que el fabricante alemán de bebidas espirituosas confirmó sus negociaciones sobre una posible oferta pública de adquisición por parte del productor de alcohol Sazerac, con sede en Nueva Orleans. * La mayor plataforma de comercio electrónico de Polonia, Allegro , revisó al alza sus previsiones para 2026 y confirmó que los resultados del segundo trimestre superaron las previsiones, lo que llevó a sus acciones a encabezar la lista de valores con mayor subida del STOXX 600, con un alza del 9,5%.

item.title: Ações sobem após alta de juros pelo Fed com recuo do petróleo e estabilização de rendimentos
item.description: As ações europeias subiram nesta quinta-feira, à medida que os preços mais baixos do petróleo e uma pausa na liquidação de títulos aumentaram o apetite por risco após o Federal Reserve ter anunciado aumento da taxa de juros nos Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: As ações europeias subiram nesta quinta-feira, à medida que os preços mais baixos do petróleo e uma pausa na liquidação de títulos aumentaram o apetite por risco após o Federal Reserve ter anunciado aumento da taxa de juros nos Estados Unidos. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) subiu 0,9%, para 642,6 pontos. As ações do setor de mineração de metais (.SXPP) lideraram os ganhos, com alta de 2,1%. As montadoras (.SXAP) subiram 1,7%, impulsionadas por ganhos de cerca de 2% da BMW (BMWG.DE) , da Renault (RENA.PA) e da Volkswagen . O petróleo Brent ampliou as perdas pelo segundo dia consecutivo após relatos de que a Arábia Saudita estava oferecendo cargas adicionais por meio de Omã, embora os preços tenham permanecido acima de US$100 o barril. O setor de energia da Europa (.SXEP) , no entanto, registrou alta de 0,1%. O primeiro aumento da taxa de juros pelo Fed em três anos, na quarta-feira, reforçou as expectativas de que os principais bancos centrais estão intensificando os esforços para conter a inflação. Os rendimentos dos Treasuries caíram nesta quinta-feira, à medida que os investidores avaliavam a decisão e os sinais de um novo aperto monetário no futuro. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) avançou 1,19%, a 10.816,14 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) subiu 0,70%, a 25.716,71 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) ganhou 0,57%, a 8.186,93 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve valorização de 0,80%, a 52.385,50 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou alta de 1,00%, a 19.831,80 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) valorizou-se 1,37%, a 9.671,11 pontos.

item.title: Republican candidate in Florida warns Trump his immigration agenda has 'gone too far'
item.description: A Latina Republican lawmaker facing a competitive reelection race in Florida warned US President Donald Trump on Thursday that his signature immigration enforcement agenda had overreached.
item.dc:creator: David Hood-Nuño
item.content:encoded: A Latina Republican lawmaker facing a competitive reelection race in Florida warned US President Donald Trump on Thursday that his signature immigration enforcement agenda had overreached. "Mr. President, some of your immigration enforcement efforts have gone too far,” U.S. Representative Maria Elvira Salazar said in a new ad . “The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today.” The 30-second ad, recorded in front of the White House in English and Spanish, is a sign that one of the issues that helped return Trump to the White House may be working against his Republican Party as it tries to retain control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Salazar, who represents the heavily Latino district in the heart of Miami that includes historic Little Havana, faces a challenge from Democrat Eliott Rodriguez, a former television news anchor. Nonpartisan analysts rate the race as "likely Republican," meaning it is somewhat competitive, though Democrats view the seat as one of their better pickup opportunities. Salazar's appeal follows months of fallout from Trump's immigration crackdown, which initially featured large-scale street-level enforcement operations in which federal agents killed two U.S. citizens in Minneapolis earlier this year. After public backlash, the administration scaled back some highly visible operations, though deportations have remained high. WANING APPROVAL RATINGS A September Reuters/Ipsos poll found 39% of Americans approved of Trump's handling of immigration, down from 50% shortly after he returned to office in January 2025. Trump's overall approval rating stood at 35% in a September 11-14 Reuters/Ipsos poll, near the lowest level of his presidency. Trump is asking voters to treat the midterms as a referendum on his presidency, [USN:L1N452102 TEXT:"sparking unease"] from some Republicans. Salazar's ad does not blame Trump directly, instead urging him to "be careful what your immigration advisers are telling you about immigration policies." The message reflects a [USN:L6N44E0W2 TEXT:"broader sentiment"] among [USN:L6N42U0T5 TEXT:"Latino voters"], especially those who backed Trump in 2024, who have grown [USN:L6N40619X TEXT:"increasingly frustrated"] with the administration's immigration policies. Other Republicans in competitive races have also taken steps to distance themselves from the president. Earlier this week, two Iowa Republicans facing tough reelection campaigns, Representatives Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks, joined Democrats in voting to limit Trump's war powers in Iran.

item.title: Russia, China end mandate for independent monitoring of UN sanctions on Iran
item.description: Russia and China ended on Thursday a United Nations Security Council mandate for the independent monitoring of international sanctions on Iran, reviving their argument that all UN measures on Tehran had been removed under a nuclear deal with world powers.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Nichols
item.content:encoded: Russia and China ended on Thursday a United Nations Security Council mandate for the independent monitoring of international sanctions on Iran, reviving their argument that all UN measures on Tehran had been removed under a nuclear deal with world powers. All UN sanctions on Iran were [USN:L5N3VE02X TEXT:"reimposed"] a year ago after France, Britain and Germany accused Tehran of violating the 2015 nuclear pact meant to prevent it from developing a nuclear weapon. Iran denies seeking nuclear weapons. This included the return of an independent panel of experts to monitor and report to the 15-member Security Council on violations and recommend further action. However, the council has been operating without a panel of experts on Iran for the past year because it has been unable to agree on their appointment, a move that must be done by consensus. Russia and China then vetoed on Thursday a resolution that would have extended the mandate for the independent monitoring of sanctions. Eleven council members voted in favor, while Pakistan and Somalia abstained. "Without an independent panel of experts, this council loses its principal source of impartial, evidence-based reporting on sanctions violations, creating a monitoring gap that only benefits the Iranian regime and those who profit from evading those measures," Deputy US Ambassador Jennifer Locetta told the council after the vote. The United States and Israel went to war with Iran seven months ago, arguing that their aim was to stop Tehran from developing a nuclear weapon. Trump withdrew the United States from the 2015 Iran nuclear deal in 2018 during his first term in office, describing the pact as "the worst deal ever." Russia and China accused their Western counterparts of politicizing the Security Council on Thursday. "We strongly urge Western colleagues to stop their very dangerous actions on the Iran front, which threaten further complication of settling of the crisis in the Persian Gulf," Russia's UN Ambassador Vassily Nebenzia told the Security Council. "The only way to resolve disagreements and to alleviate concerns ... pertaining to the Iranian nuclear program is through political and diplomatic efforts."

item.title: ＡＩ安全性巡る企業間連携、反競争的とみなさず＝米司法省高官
item.description:
Jody Godoy
[ニューヨーク １７日 ロイター] - 米司法省の反トラスト当局者は１７日、人工知能（ＡＩ）の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＡＩ安全性巡る企業間連携、反競争的とみなさず＝米司法省高官 2:10 配信

6月5日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

Jody Godoy

[ニューヨーク １７日 ロイター] - 米司法省の反トラスト当局者は１７日、人工知能（ＡＩ）の安全性を巡る競合企業間の協力について、反競争的とはみなしていないとの認識を示した。

同省の反トラスト部門を率いるウッドワード司法次官補は、「サイバーセキュリティーや安全保障に関する連携が反競争的だとは思わない」と述べた。

また、反トラスト部門は企業との協議に前向きな姿勢を示した上で、これまでのところＡＩ研究機関から反トラスト法（独占禁止法） を巡る懸念に関する会合の要請は受けていないと明らかにした。

ＡＩの安全性を巡る議論が活発化する中、アンソロピックのダリオ・アモデイ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は先週、競合企業がＡＩ開発ペースの抑制に向けた調整を行えるよう、独占禁止法上の適用除外措置を認めるべきだと訴えた。

こうした中、ＡＩ新興企業のオープンＡＩは、ＡＩの安全性向上に向け、競合するアンソロピックやアルファベット傘下のグーグル・ディープマインドと協力していることを明らかにした。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：ＡＩで相互依存強める新興企業と巨大ＩＴ コラム：ＡＩ企業の膨らむコスト負担、高品質データで争奪戦 アングル：クック氏からターナス氏へ、アップル新体制にＡＩと「脱中国」の試練 アングル：中銀の政策運営、ＡＩ普及で「ディストピア」に直面の恐れ　研究者が警鐘 アングル：世界市場が当面向き合う6つのリスク、地政学や金融政策・ＡＩなど 最終更新: 9/18(金) 2:10 ロイター

item.title: Colombia state oil firm Ecopetrol taps De La Espriella ally as chair, El Tiempo reports
item.description: Colombian state oil firm Ecopetrol has tapped Carlos Augusto Suarez, who worked on President Abelardo De La Espriella's campaign, as chairman of the board, newspaper El Tiempo reported on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombian state oil firm Ecopetrol (ECOPETROL.CN) has tapped Carlos Augusto Suarez, who worked on President Abelardo De La Espriella's campaign, as chairman of the board, newspaper El Tiempo reported on Thursday. The reshuffle would come two days after a new board was elected. Markets are still awaiting the appointment of a chief executive for the firm. Ecopetrol did not immediately respond to Reuters request for comment.

item.title: Credit Acceptance reaches $710 million predatory auto lending settlement with most US states
item.description: Credit Acceptance Corp agreed to a $710 million settlement with 40 U.S. states and Washington, D.C. to resolve charges it drove thousands of borrowers with low incomes and low credit scores into predatory auto loans it knew they could not afford.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Stempel
item.content:encoded: Credit Acceptance Corp (CACC.O) agreed to a $710 million settlement with 40 U.S. states and Washington, D.C. to resolve charges it drove thousands of borrowers with low incomes and low credit scores into predatory auto loans it knew they could not afford. The settlement announced on Thursday also resolves claims that Credit Acceptance, one of the nation's largest subprime auto lenders, helped car dealers push consumers to buy unnecessary add-on products, such as vehicle service contracts, and insurance that they did not need or were never told about. Many borrowers ended up defaulting or having their vehicles repossessed, the states said. Credit Acceptance will forgive $634 million of debt owed by more than 55,000 borrowers who took out loans between November 2015 and November 2025, pay $60 million in restitution to thousands of other borrowers, and pay a $15.5 million penalty, New York Attorney General Letitia James said. The Southfield, Michigan-based company also agreed to change its lending practices. It will warn borrowers in advance when their loans carry historically high risk of default, waive 95% of sums owed if those borrowers default within 12 or 18 months, and refrain from suing to collect the debt or selling the debt to others. “CAC preyed on consumers in New York and across the nation with false promises of affordable loans, only to exploit them with outrageous interest rates that ruined their credit and cost them their cars," James said in a statement. In one alleged instance, Credit Acceptance awarded a $260-a-month loan to a mother of two though she made just $950 per month. The company collected $8,400 from her, and her vehicle was repossessed twice, court papers show. Credit Acceptance denied wrongdoing in agreeing to settle, court papers show. It did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Thursday's settlement also resolved a lawsuit in Manhattan federal court that James and the U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau filed against Credit Acceptance in January 2023. The CFPB withdrew from that case in April 2025, calling it "consistent with principles of justice and fairness." That agency has curtailed much of its enforcement activity during U.S. President Donald Trump 's second White House term. Credit Acceptance shares were down 2.7% at $585.08 in afternoon trading.

item.title: Montadoras chinesas procuram fábricas na Europa em antecipação às regras de conteúdo local
item.description: Enquanto montadoras chinesas buscam locais de produção na Europa em antecipação às regras de conteúdo local previstas pela União Europeia, o consultor europeu da BYD afirma que sempre encontra executivos de empresas concorrentes em aeroportos que também estão em busca do mesmo objetivo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Enquanto montadoras chinesas buscam locais de produção na Europa em antecipação às regras de conteúdo local previstas pela União Europeia, o consultor europeu da BYD (002594.SZ) afirma que sempre encontra executivos de empresas concorrentes em aeroportos que também estão em busca do mesmo objetivo. Os executivos estão focados em identificar fábricas de montagem de automóveis já existentes que permitam às marcas chinesas iniciarem a produção muito mais rapidamente do que construir uma nova fábrica do zero, disse Alfredo Altavilla à Reuters. Espanha e França continuam sendo as opções “mais viáveis” para a BYD, maior fabricante de veículos elétricos da China, pois apresentam “situações decididamente mais simples”, afirmou ele. A principal consideração é quanto custa reformar o local selecionado. “Temos que encontrar algo para comprar agora e restaurá-lo com relativamente pouco dinheiro... rapidamente”, disse Altavilla na noite de quarta-feira, durante a inauguração de uma nova concessionária da marca premium Denza, da BYD, em Turim, na Itália. “Estou constantemente visitando fábricas por toda a Europa”, disse ele, acrescentando que, após o evento, pegaria um voo noturno “para a Inglaterra para visitar outra”. “Temos uma equipe muito grande que continua realizando estudos de viabilidade para todas as instalações que estamos considerando”, disse ele, reconhecendo que os concorrentes estão fazendo o mesmo. “Nos aeroportos, a gente sempre se encontra”, disse Altavilla. REGRAS DE CONTEÚDO LOCAL Fabricantes chineses já fecharam vários acordos para compartilharem linhas de produção em fábricas europeias subutilizadas pertencentes a montadoras tradicionais, incluindo Leapmotor (9863.HK) e Dongfeng (600006.SS) com Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , na Espanha e na França, respectivamente; e a Geely (0175.HK) com a Ford (F.N) na Espanha. A Chery (9973.HK) se uniu a um parceiro local para assumir uma antiga fábrica da Nissan (7201.T) na Espanha. Agora, elas estão empenhadas em uma iniciativa mais ampla para estabelecer presença industrial dentro da UE, enquanto Bruxelas trabalha nas regras do “Made in Europe”, que definirão limites mínimos de conteúdo local para veículos elétricos vendidos no bloco. Essas regras ainda estão sendo elaboradas, mas espera-se que sejam introduzidas já no próximo ano. Ao contrário de seus rivais chineses, a BYD pretende comprar, adquirir a propriedade total e reformar uma fábrica já existente para acelerar a produção localizada. A BYD está atualmente na fase inicial de produção de sua primeira fábrica europeia de automóveis, na Hungria, e espera selecionar o local para uma segunda unidade europeia até o final do ano, disse Altavilla. Olhando mais adiante, ele disse que a BYD precisará, eventualmente, de “três fábricas de montagem e uma fábrica de baterias” na Europa para sustentar suas ambições de crescimento e cumprir regras da UE. Além da Espanha e da França, outros países ainda estão sendo considerados pela BYD, disse Altavilla. A Itália, no entanto, tornou-se um “plano B” porque a Stellantis (STLAM.MI) , única grande montadora do país, não está disposta a vender nenhuma fábrica, afirmou ele. “Não posso comprar algo que não está à venda”, disse ele. (Por Giulio Piovaccari)

item.title: Milei apresenta projeto de lei para reforçar sanções às atividades nas Malvinas
item.description: O governo da Argentina apresentou um projeto de lei para reprimir as empresas que operam nas Ilhas Malvinas, o que pode agravar as tensões com o Reino Unido em relação ao território controlado pelos britânicos, mas reivindicado pela Argentina.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O governo da Argentina apresentou um projeto de lei para reprimir as empresas que operam nas Ilhas Malvinas, o que pode agravar as tensões com o Reino Unido em relação ao território controlado pelos britânicos, mas reivindicado pela Argentina. A proposta apresentada nesta quinta-feira endurece as sanções contra empresas e pessoas que participem ilegalmente de atividades nas Ilhas Malvinas e nos espaços marítimos e na plataforma continental da Argentina em “qualquer tipo de atividade voltada para a utilização de recursos naturais renováveis ou não renováveis” sem autorização das autoridades argentinas. Além disso, cria um Conselho de Segurança Nacional, liderado pelo presidente da Argentina, para supervisionar a política de segurança nacional e proteger a infraestrutura crítica e a soberania nacional. Seus sete membros incluirão o chefe de gabinete do presidente, o ministro das Relações Exteriores, o ministro da Defesa, o ministro da Economia, o secretário de Inteligência Nacional e o secretário jurídico do presidente. O projeto de lei visa “punir aqueles que exploram nossos recursos naturais ilegalmente, criar incentivos para que cessem tal conduta e fornecer ao governo nacional ferramentas para se proteger contra ameaças externas”, informou a Presidência em comunicado nesta quinta-feira. O novo projeto de lei visa reformular a legislação de 2011 com um regime mais rigoroso e sanções mais severas direcionadas às empresas, seus acionistas e fornecedores, acrescentou o comunicado. O governo argentino informou na semana passada que havia aberto processos sancionatórios contra pelo menos 60 empresas e indivíduos ligados à exploração de petróleo em alto mar nas proximidades das ilhas, que o Reino Unido chama de Ilhas Falkland. A Argentina, que invadiu as ilhas em 1982 e travou uma guerra de 10 semanas por elas antes de se render ao Reino Unido, acelerou os esforços para reprimir as empresas envolvidas no projeto petrolífero Sea Lion desde o início deste mês, quando o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, sugeriu que Washington poderia reconsiderar sua posição tradicionalmente neutra na disputa pelas Malvinas. Os comentários de Trump surgiram em meio à sua frustração com o que ele considerou um apoio limitado do Reino Unido às operações militares lideradas pelos EUA no Oriente Médio. Opositores de centro e de esquerda há muito acusam Milei de não fazer o suficiente para defender a reivindicação da Argentina sobre as Malvinas e agora afirmam que ele está agindo por motivos políticos, visando uma provável candidatura à reeleição em 2027. Os proprietários do projeto offshore Sea Lion, a Navitas Petroleum (NVPTp.TA) e a Rockhopper Exploration (RKH.L) , afirmaram que o projeto do campo de petróleo possui licenças válidas concedidas pelo governo das Ilhas Malvinas e indicaram que não esperam que as ações de Milei prejudiquem o desenvolvimento do projeto.

item.title: Copper rallies as Chinese buyers return to market, demand outlook brightens
item.description: Copper prices rose 1.6% on the LME as Chinese buyers returned after a selloff, while stronger physical demand and a softer dollar supported the metal ...
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Copper prices rallied on Thursday as Chinese buyers returned to the market after a recent selloff while demand prospects brightened and the dollar softened. Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 1.6 per cent at $14,456 a metric tonne at 1328 GMT. Prices of the metal, used in the power and construction industries, have dropped around 4 per cent since hitting a record high of $14,875 a tonne on September 10. The dollar rose after the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates and reaffirmed its commitment to curbing inflation. But later in the session it retreated as oil prices extended their decline. A softer US currency makes dollar-priced metals cheaper for holders of other currencies, which would boost demand.Chinese buyers are back though volumes are not “massive”, said Alastair Munro, senior base metals strategist at Marex. He said Chinese demand was real physical buying, not just speculation. Strong physical demand in the top consumer can be seen in the Yangshan copper premium, a gauge of Chinese demand for copper imports, which rose to $118 a tonne on Wednesday, its highest since October 2022. It is also reflected in higher domestic physical market premiums, paid over the prices traded on the Shanghai Futures Exchange, which climbed to 645 yuan a tonne on Wednesday, its highest since December 2023. Adding  to the angst are Chinese stocks in warehouses monitored by ShFE at 54,780 tonnes, the lowest since January 2024, partly due to traders and producers shipping metal to the United States on the expectation of import tariffs. The flow of copper to the US is also why stocks in LME warehouses have dropped since February last year when President Donald Trump first talked about a levy on imports. Elsewhere, zinc climbed 1.9 per cent to $3,884 a tonne after reports of an industrial accident at Korea Zinc’s Onsan smelter raised concerns about supply. In other metals, aluminium rose 0.5 per cent to $3,285, lead gained 1 per cent to $1,905, tin advanced 1.2 per cent to $53,055 and nickel added 1.1 per cent to $16,350.

item.title: J.P.Morgan sees BoE hiking rates in February
item.description: J.P.Morgan expects the Bank of England to raise interest rates by 25 basis points in February, following the central bank's decision to keep borrowing costs on hold, but warns of further tightening if the Iran war continues.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: J.P.Morgan expects the Bank of England to raise interest rates by 25 basis points in February, following the central bank's decision to keep borrowing costs on [USN:L8N4590W3 TEXT:"hold"], but warns of further tightening if the Iran war continues. The UK central bank's [USN:L8N4590W3 TEXT:"Monetary Policy Committee"] voted 6-3 to keep rates at 3.75% earlier on Thursday, but also predicted that inflation could top 4% early next year. "It almost sounds as if they have already made up their minds on a November hike provided there are no material changes in the geopolitical outlook," Allan Monks, a senior economist at J.P.Morgan, said in a note. Monks expects a rate hike in November and another one in 2027. Following this he expects the BoE to stay put on borrowing costs, unless there is clearer evidence of a second round of inflation effects such as wage expectations rising to 4%. He previously expected the central bank to hike rates once in November 2026 and then reduce rates twice in 2027. Along with the rate decision, the BoE also [USN:L8N4590WV TEXT:"paused its sales"] of government bonds for six months and it began a longer-term overhaul of how it shrinks its debt holdings. The announcement sent bond yields lower and came ahead of the Andy Burnham government's keenly awaited budget next month at a time when global fixed-income investors are concerned about soaring developed market debt. "This is a clear and assertive plan designed to reduce uncertainty at a time when market conditions are volatile," J.P.Morgan said. "This is a big surprise given the associated optics of blurring the line between BoE and government decisions."

item.title: Italy readies navy to protect its shipping amid Bab el-Mandeb tensions
item.description: Italy is preparing for a possible naval mission to safeguard its merchant shipping as security concerns mount in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy is preparing for a possible naval mission to safeguard its merchant shipping as [USN:L6N4561AA TEXT:"security concerns mount"] in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said on Thursday. Crosetto said he and Italy's chief of defence staff had agreed to mobilise the navy to prepare "whatever is necessary" to guarantee the secure transit of Italian vessels, arguing that delays in responding to mounting maritime risks could have direct consequences for the economy and consumers. Fears for shipping in the Red Sea have surged this month after the Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of parts of Yemen's coast that overlook the Bab el-Mandeb, threatening Saudi oil exports rerouted from the Strait of Hormuz. "I have decided ... to activate the Italian navy to prepare what is necessary to guarantee the safe transit of Italian ships," Crosetto said in a statement. "We cannot allow bureaucratic delays in decision-making to aggravate an already complex situation, with direct consequences for our economy and the lives of our citizens." He did not spell out what measures were being considered or what naval assets might be sent to the area. Crosetto said that disruptions to major shipping lanes would drive up transport costs, delay deliveries and ultimately push higher prices onto families and businesses. "Every economic crisis hits the most vulnerable people hardest, putting social cohesion and the country's stability at risk," he said. The defence minister also highlighted the vulnerability of undersea infrastructure, including data cables and energy links. "For a major maritime nation such as Italy, monitoring and protecting the seas, both above and below the surface, means safeguarding its security, its prosperity and its future," he said. "The defence ministry and the Italian navy will continue to protect the sea, intervening with determination whenever necessary to safeguard national interests and the security of Italians," he said.

item.title: US Democrats look to stop Trump's Saudi nuclear deal
item.description: US House of Representatives Democrats raised concerns on Thursday about President Donald Trump's civil nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia, and said they had introduced a resolution of disapproval seeking to block the deal from coming into force.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: US House of Representatives Democrats raised concerns on Thursday about President Donald Trump's civil nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia, and said they had introduced a resolution of disapproval seeking to block the deal from coming into force. Trump [USN:L1N44M100 TEXT:"sent the proposed agreement"] to Congress in August, opening a 90-day window for lawmakers' review and giving them an opportunity to try to pass a resolution of disapproval. Democrats and nonproliferation advocates have criticized the nuclear pact for not barring Saudi Arabia from enriching uranium or reprocessing nuclear waste, two potential pathways to a nuclear weapon. The United Arab Emirates agreed to such measures, known as the gold standard, in its 2009 civil nuclear deal with Washington. "A region already gripped by conflict and escalation does not need another nuclear power," the four Democrats — Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee; Brad Sherman and John Garamendi of California, and Don Beyer of Virginia — said in a statement. The Trump administration says the deal has nonproliferation measures required by law. It is not clear whether Saudi Arabia will get the deal without normalizing relations with Israel. Trump has said the pact will only go into effect if Riyadh does so, but congressional aides said there is nothing in the agreement addressing that issue. Members of Congress [USN:L1N4580MN TEXT:"have also called"] for all of the agreement — including classified "side letters" reached with Saudi Arabia — to be made public. The 30-year nuclear deal calls for the construction of AP1000 reactors, a project worth tens of billions of dollars that would benefit Westinghouse, jointly owned by Canada-based Cameco (CCO.TO) and Brookfield Asset Management (BAM.N) . It is unclear when the House might vote on the resolution. Speaker Mike Johnson on Wednesday sent members home until after the November 3 midterm elections. Additionally, while Congress has passed dozens of disapproval resolutions over the years, no resolution regarding nuclear power or civil nuclear cooperation has ever successfully passed. Under Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, agreements for peaceful nuclear cooperation automatically go into effect after 90 days if Congress has not passed a disapproval resolution to block them.

item.title: Escrito judicial cita comentarios de Trump y una foto en la que se lee "Kennedy Center DEMOLIDO"
item.description: Los abogados que luchan por mantener abierto el Kennedy Center e impedir que el nombre de Donald Trump figure en su fachada presentaron el jueves nuevas pruebas, citando los comentarios del presidente de Estados Unidos y una fotografía en la que se alude a la demolición del centro de artes escénicas.
item.dc:creator: Katharine Jackson, Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: Los abogados que luchan por mantener abierto el Kennedy Center e impedir que el nombre de Donald Trump figure en su fachada presentaron el jueves nuevas pruebas, citando los comentarios del presidente de Estados Unidos y una fotografía en la que se alude a la demolición del centro de artes escénicas. En un escrito judicial, los abogados de la demandante, la congresista Joyce Beatty, demócrata por Ohio, informaron al tribunal de los comentarios que el presidente hizo el miércoles por la noche. "Creo que la Administración Trump debería recibir sin duda un reconocimiento. Porque, francamente, si no lo hacemos, va a cerrar. Acabará siendo demolido", declaró Trump a los periodistas en Carolina del Norte. Los abogados también citaron una foto que circulaba por las redes sociales en la que se veía al presidente a bordo del Air Force One mirando un cartel que, según ellos, parecía llevar el título "Kennedy Center DEMOLIDO". La foto no pudo ser verificada de forma independiente por Reuters. Beatty ha solicitado al juez federal de distrito Christopher Cooper, con sede en Washington, que celebre una audiencia de urgencia sobre la demanda después de que la junta directiva del Kennedy Center —incluidos Trump y los miembros designados por él mismo— votara esta semana a favor de cerrar el centro durante un máximo de dos años para llevar a cabo un proyecto de renovación de 257 millones de dólares. Afirmó que el Kennedy Center, creado por el Congreso e inaugurado en 1971 en Washington, D.C., como homenaje al expresidente John F. Kennedy, ya no es accesible al público durante el horario habitual de apertura. El miércoles se podían ver nuevas barreras en el exterior del edificio. Cooper ordenó a la junta que explique antes del jueves si el plan infringe una orden previa suya que limitaba su capacidad para cerrar las puertas. La junta afirmó el jueves por la mañana que no se estaba infringiendo la orden y que un responsable del centro cerró el miércoles para llevar a cabo reparaciones de emergencia durante siete días. La Administración Trump afirmó que solicitará al juez, antes del viernes, que revoque la orden anterior para permitir lo que el Gobierno denominó "el cierre necesario para completar la restauración y las renovaciones".

item.title: ULTIM'ORA MEDIO ORIENTE: Missione Onu indica crimini guerra Usa in Iran
item.description: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sulla situazione in Medio Oriente:
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sulla situazione in Medio Oriente: 17.50 - Secondo una missione di accertamento delle Nazioni Unite sull’Iran, ci sarebbero motivi ragionevoli per ritenere che gli Stati Uniti siano responsabili di due attacchi militari contro una scuola e un impianto sportivo avvenuti in Iran a febbraio e che tali attacchi costituiscano crimini di guerra. La stessa missione ritiene che le autorità iraniane abbiano commesso crimini contro l’umanità durante la sanguinosa repressione delle proteste antigovernative. 13.15 - I leader militari europei e arabi si incontrano a Parigi per valutare le necessità delle Forze armate libanesi, e discutere l'imminente conclusione della missione di peacekeeping delle Nazioni Unite, dati i crescenti timori di una rinnovata campagna militare di Israele nel Libano meridionale. I colloqui di oggi - inizialmente gestiti dal presidente francese Emmanuel Macron insieme al presidente libanese Joseph Aoun e al re di Giordania Abdullah - non fanno parte degli sforzi di Washington per alleviare le tensioni lungo il confine tra Israele e Libano. Gli Stati Uniti saranno rappresentati da un alto funzionario militare coinvolto in questioni di sicurezza in Medio Oriente.

item.title: 'I'm Russian,' Ovechkin says about decision to appear in ad for Putin-backed United Russia
item.description: Alexander Ovechkin said on Thursday that he agreed to appear in a political campaign advertisement for the United Russia party, which is backed by President Vladimir Putin, because he supports his country.
item.dc:creator: Brad Ulery
item.content:encoded: Alexander Ovechkin said on Thursday that he agreed to appear in a political campaign advertisement for the United Russia party, which is backed by President Vladimir Putin, because he supports his country. "I'm Russian, and I support my country," Ovechkin, the NHL's all-time leading goalscorer, told reporters at the Washington Capitals' media day. "I'm for peace and love, and I hope in the world it doesn't matter who you are, I hope everybody understands, everybody wants peace and everybody hope everything is going to be okay in the world." Russia will hold a parliamentary election from September 18 to 20, the first since it launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022. Ovechkin, who can be seen standing behind Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in the video, said he was asked to participate and did not hesitate to agree. He added that he will live in Russia following the end of his career. "As soon as I'm done playing hockey, I'm probably going to stay there," he said. "I'm gonna live there, my kids gonna live there, family. I'm for peace and love and I hope everything's going to be okay." Ovechkin has faced scrutiny over his longstanding ties to Putin as Russia wages war in Ukraine. In 2017 he formed a [USN:KBN1D22LC TEXT:"public movement"] in support of Putin and his Instagram profile picture is a photo of him and the Russian president. He [USN:L1N2V03AT TEXT:"called for peace"] in February 2022 following his home country's invasion of Ukraine. When asked about his support for Putin at the time, he said, "Well, he is my president. But ... I am not in politics. I am an athlete and ... I hope everything is going to be done soon." Ovechkin, who turned 41 on Thursday, has scored 929 goals in 1,573 regular-season NHL games and the upcoming season will be his 22nd in the league. He led the Capitals to a Stanley Cup in 2018.
